units.zh: 萇從簡，陳州人也。
units.en: Chang Congjian was from Chenzhou.
units.literal: Chang Congjian was a native of Chenzhou.

units.zh: 世以屠羊為業，力敵數人，善用槊。
units.en: His family had butchered sheep for generations; he had the strength of several men and was a skilled spearman.
units.literal: His family for generations made their living butchering sheep; his strength matched several men, and he was skilled with the spear.

units.zh: 初事後唐莊宗為小校，每遇攻城，召人為梯頭，從簡多應募焉，莊宗為其勇，擢領帳前親衛兼步軍都指揮使。
units.en: He first served Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong as a junior officer. Whenever a siege called for volunteers to lead the ladder teams, Congjian often stepped forward; Zhuangzong admired his daring and promoted him to command the imperial guard before the tent and the palace infantry as well.
units.literal: At first he served Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong as a junior officer; whenever a city was besieged and men were called to lead the ladder assaults, Congjian often volunteered; Zhuangzong admired his courage and promoted him to command the personal guard before the tent and concurrently to be commander of the palace guard infantry.

units.zh: 一日，莊宗領大軍與梁軍對陣，登高丘而坐，敵人有執大幟揚其武者，莊宗指之謂左右曰：「猛士也。」
units.en: One day Zhuangzong drew up his main force against the Liang army and sat on a high mound to watch. An enemy soldier was flourishing a great banner to show his prowess. Zhuangzong pointed him out and said to his attendants, "There is a fierce fighter."
units.literal: One day Zhuangzong led a great army to face the Liang army in battle array; he sat atop a high mound, and among the enemy was one who held a great banner and displayed his martial prowess. Zhuangzong pointed at him and said to those beside him, "A fierce warrior."

units.zh: 從簡曰：「臣為大王取之。」
units.en: Congjian said, "I will bring that banner back for you, my lord."
units.literal: Congjian said, "Your servant will take it for the Great King."

units.zh: 莊宗慮其不捷，不許。
units.en: Zhuangzong feared he would fail and refused permission.
units.literal: Zhuangzong feared he would not succeed and did not permit it.

units.zh: 從簡退，乃潛領十數騎挺身而入，奪幟以歸，萬眾鼓噪，莊宗壯之，錫賚甚厚。
units.en: Congjian withdrew, then secretly led a dozen horsemen straight into the enemy line, seized the banner, and rode back. The whole army erupted in cheers. Zhuangzong was deeply impressed and rewarded him lavishly.
units.literal: Congjian withdrew, then secretly led a dozen or so horsemen and charged straight in, seized the banner, and returned; the myriad hosts roared approval, Zhuangzong found him magnificent, and bestowed rewards very generously.

units.zh: 又嘗中箭而鏃入於骨，使醫工出之，以刃鑿骨，恐其痛也，良久未能搖動。
units.en: On another occasion an arrow struck him and the head lodged in the bone. A physician tried to extract it by chiseling the bone with a blade, hesitating for fear of the pain, and for a long time could not work it loose.
units.literal: On another occasion he was struck by an arrow and the arrowhead lodged in the bone; he had a physician extract it, using a blade to chisel the bone, fearing the pain, and for a long time could not get it to budge.

units.zh: 從簡嗔目謂曰：「何不沈鑿？」
units.en: Congjian glared at him and said, "Why not strike the chisel home?"
units.literal: Congjian glared and said, "Why not drive the chisel in hard?"

units.zh: 洎出之，左右無不惻然，從簡顏色自若，其勇壯皆此類也。
units.en: When the head was finally out, everyone around him winced, but Congjian's face never changed. His courage was always of this kind.
units.literal: When it was finally extracted, none of those beside him were not moved to pity, yet Congjian's countenance was as calm as ever; his courage and toughness were all of this sort.

units.zh: 從簡所為多不法，莊宗以其戰鬥多捷，常屈法赦之。
units.en: Congjian often acted outside the law, but Zhuangzong, because he won battle after battle, regularly bent the rules to spare him.
units.literal: Much of what Congjian did was unlawful, but Zhuangzong, because he won many battles, often bent the law to pardon him.

units.zh: 賜姓，名曰紹瓊。
units.en: He was granted the imperial surname and took the name Shaoqiong.
units.literal: He was granted the imperial surname and given the name Shaoqiong.

units.zh: 後加竭誠匡國功臣，累官至金紫光祿大夫、檢校太保、景州刺史，歷洺州團練使。
units.en: He was later made a Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty in Restoring the State, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Ribbon and Acting Grand Guardian, served as prefect of Jingzhou, and was military training commissioner of Mingzhou.
units.literal: Later he was given the title Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty in Restoring the State, rose through offices to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Golden Seal and Ribbon and Acting Grand Guardian, and served as prefect of Jingzhou and as military training commissioner of Mingzhou.

units.zh: 及梁平，典蔡州。
units.en: After the Liang was subdued, he governed Caizhou.
units.literal: When Liang was pacified, he was put in charge of Caizhou.

units.zh: 同光四年，授許州節度使，會莊宗晏駕，未及赴鎮而止。
units.en: In the fourth year of Tongguang he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, but Zhuangzong died before he could take up the post, and the appointment came to nothing.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tongguang he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, but when Zhuangzong died he had not yet reached his post and the appointment lapsed.

units.zh: 明宗登極，例復本姓，歷麟、汝、汾、金四州刺史。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he resumed his original surname as was customary and served in turn as prefect of Lin, Ru, Fen, and Jin.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong ascended the throne, by precedent he resumed his original surname and served in turn as prefect of Lin, Ru, Fen, and Jin prefectures.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：明宗尤惡貪貨，面戒汝州刺史萇從簡，為其貪暴。）〉
units.en: (Scattered Words from Northern Dreams records that Emperor Mingzong especially hated greed; he personally warned Chang Congjian, prefect of Ru, for his rapacity.)
units.literal: (Scattered Words from Northern Dreams records: Emperor Mingzong especially hated greed for goods; he personally admonished Chang Congjian, prefect of Ruzhou, for his greed and cruelty.)

units.zh: 應順初，舉軍伐鳳翔，從簡亦預其行，會軍變，乃東還。
units.en: Early in Yingshun the court marched against Fengxiang, and Congjian went with the expedition, but when the army mutinied he turned back east.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun the army was raised to attack Fengxiang; Congjian also took part in the campaign, but when the army mutinied he returned east.

units.zh: 道遇張廷蘊，為廷蘊所執，送於末帝。
units.en: On the road he met Zhang Tingyun, who seized him and sent him to the Last Emperor.
units.literal: On the road he met Zhang Tingyun, was seized by Tingyun, and sent to the Last Emperor.

units.zh: 末帝數之曰：「人皆歸我，爾何背我而去也？」
units.en: The Last Emperor rebuked him: "Everyone else has come to me. Why did you turn your back and leave?"
units.literal: The Last Emperor reproached him, saying, "All others have come over to me—why did you turn your back and leave?"

units.zh: 從簡曰：「事主不敢二心，今日死生惟命。」
units.en: Congjian said, "A loyal servant does not waver. Today my life is in your hands."
units.literal: Congjian said, "In serving one's lord one dares not have two hearts; today life or death is yours to command."

units.zh: 末帝釋之。
units.en: The Last Emperor let him go.
units.literal: The Last Emperor released him.

units.zh: 清泰二年，授潁州團練使。
units.en: In the second year of Qingtai he became military training commissioner of Yingzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he was appointed military training commissioner of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 高祖舉義，末帝將議親征，詔赴闕，充副招討使，隨駕至孟津，除河陽節度使。
units.en: When Gaozu rose in revolt, the Last Emperor prepared to take the field in person. Congjian was summoned to court as deputy pacification commissioner, accompanied the emperor to Mengjin, and was appointed military commissioner of Heyang.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised the banner of revolt, the Last Emperor was about to discuss a personal campaign; Congjian was summoned to court, appointed deputy pacification commissioner, accompanied the imperial carriage to Mengjin, and was made military commissioner of Heyang.

units.zh: 及趙延壽軍敗，斷浮橋歸洛，留從簡守河陽。
units.en: After Zhao Yanshou's defeat the pontoon bridge was cut and the court fled back to Luoyang, leaving Congjian to defend Heyang.
units.literal: When Zhao Yanshou's army was defeated, the pontoon bridge was cut and the court returned to Luoyang, leaving Congjian to hold Heyang.

units.zh: 高祖自北而至，從簡察軍情離散，遂渡河迎謁高祖。
units.en: When Gaozu advanced from the north, Congjian saw that the army was falling apart, crossed the river, and went to submit to him.
units.literal: Gaozu came from the north; Congjian saw that the army's morale was scattered, crossed the river, and went to pay homage to Gaozu.

units.zh: 天福元年十二月，授許州節度使，改賜推忠佐運保國功臣。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu he was made military commissioner of Xu Prefecture and granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Pushes Loyalty, Assists the Mandate, and Guards the State.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture and granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Pushes Loyalty, Assists the Mandate, and Guards the State.

units.zh: 二年秋，移鎮徐州。
units.en: In the autumn of the second year he was transferred to Xuzhou.
units.literal: In the autumn of the second year he was transferred to command Xuzhou.

units.zh: 三年，加開府儀同三司、檢校太尉，進封開國公，食邑至一千五百戶。
units.en: In the third year he was made Grand General with Honored Ceremonials Equal to the Three Excellencies and Acting Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke Who Founds the State, and granted a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
units.literal: In the third year he was given the rank of Grand General with Honored Ceremonials Equal to the Three Excellencies and Acting Grand Commandant, advanced to Duke Who Founds the State, and his fief reached one thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 受代歸闕，授左金吾衛上將軍。
units.en: When his term ended he returned to court and was appointed senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
units.literal: When relieved and returned to court, he was appointed senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

units.zh: 從簡性忌刻而多疑，歷州鎮凡十餘，所在豎棘於公署，才通人行，左右稍違忤，即加鞭笞，或至殺害，其意不可測，吏人皆側行。
units.en: Congjian was jealous, harsh, and suspicious. In more than ten prefectures and circuits he planted thorn hedges in his offices so that only one man could pass at a time. The slightest disobedience from an attendant brought a flogging, sometimes death. No one could guess his mood, and his staff crept along the walls.
units.literal: Congjian by nature was jealous, harsh, and suspicious; over more than ten prefectures and circuits he served, wherever he was he set up thorn hedges in the government offices so that only a single person could pass; if those beside him showed the slightest disobedience he at once had them flogged, and sometimes even killed; his intent could not be fathomed, and clerks and subordinates all walked sideways.

units.zh: 其煩苛暴虐，為武臣之最。
units.en: Among the military governors his petty cruelty was unmatched.
units.literal: His vexatious severity and cruelty were the worst among military men.

units.zh: 六年秋，隨駕幸鄴都，遇疾請告，尋卒於鄉里，年六十五。
units.en: In the autumn of the sixth year he accompanied the emperor to Yedu, fell ill and asked for leave, and soon died at home, aged sixty-five.
units.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he accompanied the imperial progress to Yedu, fell ill and requested leave, and soon died in his home district at the age of sixty-five.

units.zh: 贈太傅。
units.en: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
units.literal: He was posthumously given the title Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 潘環，字楚奇，洛陽人也。
units.en: Pan Huan, courtesy name Chuqi, was from Luoyang.
units.literal: Pan Huan, courtesy name Chuqi, was a native of Luoyang.

units.zh: 父景厚，以環貴，授左監門上將軍致仕。
units.en: His father Jinghou, because of Huan's rank, was made senior general of the Left Gate Guard and allowed to retire.
units.literal: His father Jinghou, because of Huan's eminence, was granted the post of senior general of the Left Gate Guard and retired from office.

units.zh: 環少以負販為業，始事梁邢州節度使閻寶，為帳中親校。
units.en: As a young man he peddled goods for a living. He first served Yan Bao, Liang's military commissioner of Xingzhou, as a personal attendant in the command tent.
units.literal: In youth Huan made his living as a peddler; he first served Yan Bao, military commissioner of Xingzhou under Liang, as a personal attendant in the tent.

units.zh: 及莊宗定魏博，移兵攻邢，寶遣環間道馳奏於梁，梁末帝用為左堅銳夾馬都虞候，累遷左雄威指揮使。
units.en: When Zhuangzong subdued Weibo and marched on Xing, Bao sent Huan by a secret route to report to Liang. The Last Emperor of Liang made him chief adjutant of the Left Firm and Sharp Horse-Flanking Corps and later promoted him to commander of the Left Majestic Might Corps.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Weibo and shifted troops to attack Xing, Bao sent Huan by a secret route to report urgently to Liang; the Last Emperor of Liang employed him as chief adjutant of the Left Firm and Sharp Horse-Flanking Corps and repeatedly promoted him to commander of the Left Majestic Might Corps.

units.zh: 時梁人與莊宗對壘於河上，環每預戰，先登陷敵，金瘡遍體。
units.en: While Liang and Zhuangzong faced each other along the Yellow River, Huan fought in every engagement, was always first over the wall, and bore blade wounds all over his body.
units.literal: At that time the Liang and Zhuangzong faced each other in battle array along the Yellow River; Huan took part in every fight, was first to scale the walls and break the enemy, and wounds from blades covered his whole body.

units.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》云：潘環常中流矢於面，骨銜其鏃，故負重傷。
units.en: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall records that Pan Huan was once struck in the face by an arrow whose head lodged in the bone, inflicting a grave wound.
units.literal: (Idle Talk from the Jade Hall records: Pan Huan was often struck in the face by a flying arrow; the bone gripped the arrowhead, so he bore a grave wound.

units.zh: 醫療至經年，其鏃自出，其瘡成漏，終身不痊。）〉
units.en: Treatment lasted nearly a year before the head worked itself free, but the wound became a fistula and never fully healed.)
units.literal: Medical treatment lasted nearly a year; the arrowhead came out on its own, the wound became a fistula, and he never healed for the rest of his life.)

units.zh: 莊宗知其名，及平梁，命典禁軍。
units.en: Zhuangzong knew his name, and after Liang fell he put him in charge of the palace guard.
units.literal: Zhuangzong knew his reputation, and when Liang was pacified appointed him to command the palace guard.

units.zh: 同光中，從明宗北禦契丹，鄴軍之亂，從明宗入洛。
units.en: During Tongguang he marched north with Mingzong against the Khitan, and when the Yedu army mutinied he followed Mingzong into Luoyang.
units.literal: During Tongguang he followed Mingzong north to resist the Khitan; when the Yedu army mutinied he followed Mingzong into Luoyang.

units.zh: 天成初，授棣州刺史。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he became prefect of Dizhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Dizhou.

units.zh: 會定州王都反，朝廷攻之，以環為行營右廂步軍都指揮使。
units.en: When Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled and the court marched against him, Huan was made commander of the campaign's right-wing infantry.
units.literal: When Wang Du of Dingzhou rebelled and the court attacked him, Huan was made commander of the right wing infantry of the campaign headquarters.

units.zh: 賊平，改易州刺史、北面沿邊都部署，後移刺慶州。
units.en: After the rebellion was crushed he became prefect of Yizhou and overall frontier deployment commissioner on the northern border, and later was transferred to Qing Prefecture.
units.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was made prefect of Yizhou and overall frontier deployment commissioner for the northern border, and later transferred to govern Qing Prefecture.

units.zh: 受代歸闕，明宗召對，顧侍臣曰：「此人勇敢，少能偕者。」
units.en: When his term ended he returned to court. Mingzong received him and told his ministers, "This man is brave. Few can match him."
units.literal: When relieved and returned to court, Mingzong summoned him for an audience and, turning to the attending ministers, said, "This man is brave; few can match him."

units.zh: 尋除宿州團練使。
units.en: Soon afterward he was made military training commissioner of Suzhou.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed military training commissioner of Suzhou.

units.zh: 清泰中，移耀州。
units.en: During Qingtai he was transferred to Yaozhou.
units.literal: During Qingtai he was transferred to Yaozhou.

units.zh: 天福中，預平範延光，授齊州防禦使。
units.en: During Tianfu he helped suppress Fan Yanguang and was made defense commissioner of Qizhou.
units.literal: During Tianfu he took part in pacifying Fan Yanguang and was appointed defense commissioner of Qizhou.

units.zh: 四年，升金州為節鎮，以環為節度使，久之，入為左神武統軍。
units.en: In the fourth year Jinzhou was elevated to a full circuit, and Huan became its military commissioner. After some years he returned to court as commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.
units.literal: In the fourth year Jinzhou was elevated to a circuit command; Huan was made its military commissioner, and after a long time entered court as commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.

units.zh: 開運初，契丹入寇，王師北征，以環為北面行營步軍左廂排陣使，預破契丹於陽城。
units.en: Early in Kaiyun the Khitan invaded and the court marched north. Huan was made battle-array commissioner of the northern campaign's left-wing infantry and helped defeat the Khitan at Yangcheng.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun the Khitan invaded; the imperial army marched north, and Huan was made battle-array commissioner of the left wing infantry of the northern campaign headquarters; he took part in defeating the Khitan at Yangcheng.

units.zh: 軍回，授澶州節度使，累官至檢校太傅。
units.en: When the army returned he was made military commissioner of Chanzhou and eventually rose to Acting Grand Mentor.
units.literal: When the army returned he was appointed military commissioner of Chanzhou and rose through offices to Acting Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 三年，罷鎮歸闕，俄受詔洛京巡檢。
units.en: In the third year he left his post and returned to court, and soon received orders as patrol commissioner of the Luoyang capital.
units.literal: In the third year he left his command and returned to court; soon he received orders as patrol commissioner of the Luoyang capital.

units.zh: 其年冬，戎王犯闕，偽署劉晞為西京留守，環乞罷巡警，閑居洛陽。
units.en: That winter the Khitan ruler stormed the capital and installed Liu Xi as regent of the Western Capital. Huan asked to be relieved of patrol duty and lived quietly in Luoyang.
units.literal: That winter the barbarian king violated the capital; he falsely appointed Liu Xi as Western Capital regent; Huan begged to be relieved of patrol duty and lived at leisure in Luoyang.

units.zh: 遇河陽軍亂，晞出奔，未幾，蕃將高牟翰以兵援晞入於洛，慮環有變，乃害之，盡取其家財。
units.en: When the Heyang garrison mutinied, Xi fled. Soon the Khitan general Gao Mouhan marched into Luoyang to support him, feared Huan might turn against them, killed him, and seized his entire estate.
units.literal: When the Heyang army mutinied, Xi fled; before long the barbarian general Gao Mouhan brought troops to support Xi into Luoyang, feared that Huan might turn against them, killed him, and took all his household wealth.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：晞疑環構其眾逐己，使牟翰殺之。）〉
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that Xi suspected Huan had turned the troops against him and had Mouhan kill him.)
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror records: Xi suspected that Huan had incited the troops to drive him out and had Mouhan kill him.)

units.zh: 漢高祖至京，贈太尉。
units.en: When Han Gaozu reached the capital, Huan was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu reached the capital, Huan was posthumously given the title Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 環歷六部兩鎮，所至以聚斂為務。
units.en: Huan served in six ministries and two circuits, and everywhere he went his chief business was extortion.
units.literal: Huan served in six ministries and two circuits; wherever he went he made extortion his business.

units.zh: 在宿州時，有牙將因微過見怒，環紿言笞之，牙校因托一尼嘗熟於環者，獻白金兩鋌。
units.en: At Suzhou a junior officer provoked him over a minor fault. Huan pretended he would have him flogged, and the adjutant, through a nun who knew Huan well, offered two ingots of silver.
units.literal: While at Suzhou a junior general angered him over a trifling fault; Huan pretended he would have him flogged, and the adjutant, through a nun who was on familiar terms with Huan, presented two ingots of white silver.

units.zh: 尼詣環白牙校餉𨫼腳兩枚，求免其責，環曰：「𨫼本幾腳？」
units.en: The nun told Huan the adjutant had sent two ingot-feet as a gift and begged mercy. Huan asked, "How many feet does a full ingot have?"
units.literal: The nun went to Huan and reported that the adjutant had sent two ingot-feet as a gift, asking to be spared punishment. Huan said, "How many feet does an ingot have in the first place?"

units.zh: 尼曰：「三腳。」
units.en: The nun said, "Three feet."
units.literal: The nun said, "Three feet."

units.zh: 環復曰：「今兩腳能成𨫼乎？」
units.en: Huan said, "Can two feet make a whole ingot?"
units.literal: Huan said again, "Can two feet make a complete ingot now?"

units.zh: 尼則以三數致之，當時號環為「潘𨫼腳」。
units.en: The nun then sent three. People nicknamed him "Pan Ingot-Feet."
units.literal: The nun then sent the full count of three, and at the time Huan was nicknamed "Pan Ingot-Feet."

units.zh: 方太，字伯宗，青州千乘人也。
units.en: Fang Tai, courtesy name Bozong, was from Qiansheng in Qingzhou.
units.literal: Fang Tai, courtesy name Bozong, was a native of Qiansheng in Qingzhou.

units.zh: 少隸本軍為小校，嘗戍登州，劫海客，事泄，刺史淳於晏匿之，遇赦免。
units.en: As a youth he served in the local army as a junior officer. While garrisoning Dengzhou he robbed seagoing merchants; when the affair came out, Prefect Chunyu Yan sheltered him, and he was spared by an amnesty.
units.literal: In youth he served in the local army as a junior officer; he once garrisoned Dengzhou and robbed seafaring merchants; when the affair was exposed, Prefect Chunyu Yan hid him, and he was spared by an amnesty.

units.zh: 事定州節度使楊光遠，光遠領兵赴晉陽。
units.en: He served Yang Guangyuan, military commissioner of Dingzhou, when Guangyuan marched on Jinyang.
units.literal: He served Yang Guangyuan, military commissioner of Dingzhou; Guangyuan led troops to Jinyang.

units.zh: 本州軍亂，太與馬萬、盧順密等擒之，使太縛送至闕。
units.en: The local army mutinied. Tai, Ma Wan, Lu Shunmi, and others seized Guangyuan and had Tai bind him and escort him to court.
units.literal: The army of the prefecture mutinied; Tai, together with Ma Wan, Lu Shunmi, and others seized him, and had Tai bind him and send him to court.

units.zh: 尋從杜重威破張從賓於汜水，以功除趙州刺史。
units.en: He soon followed Du Chongwei in defeating Zhang Congbin at Sishui and, for his service, was made prefect of Zhaozhou.
units.literal: Soon afterward he followed Du Chongwei in defeating Zhang Congbin at Sishui and, for merit, was made prefect of Zhaozhou.

units.zh: 從楊光遠平範延光於鄴，移刺萊州，遷安州防禦使。
units.en: He followed Yang Guangyuan in suppressing Fan Yanguang at Ye, was transferred to Laizhou, and became defense commissioner of Anzhou.
units.literal: He followed Yang Guangyuan in pacifying Fan Yanguang at Ye, was transferred to govern Laizhou, and was promoted to defense commissioner of Anzhou.

units.zh: 從少帝幸澶州，與契丹戰於戚城，中數創，改鳳州防禦使，行至中途，遷河陽留後，移邢州留後。
units.en: He accompanied the Young Emperor to Chanzhou and fought the Khitan at Qicheng, where he was wounded several times. He was made defense commissioner of Fengzhou, then, before reaching his post, was transferred to acting regent of Heyang and then of Xingzhou.
units.literal: He accompanied the Young Emperor to Chanzhou, fought the Khitan at Qicheng, received several wounds, was made defense commissioner of Fengzhou, and while still on the road was transferred to acting regent of Heyang and then acting regent of Xingzhou.

units.zh: 契丹犯闕，偽命遙領洋州節度使，充洛京巡檢，與前洺州團練使李瓊俱至鄭州，其屯駐兵士迫請太在城巡檢，以備外盜，號為「鄭王」。
units.en: When the Khitan stormed the capital he was falsely named titular military commissioner of Yangzhou and patrol commissioner of Luoyang. He and Li Qiong, former military training commissioner of Ming, reached Zhengzhou, where the garrison pressed him to patrol the city against outside raiders and called him "King of Zheng."
units.literal: When the Khitan violated the capital, by a false appointment he was made titular military commissioner of Yangzhou and patrol commissioner of the Luoyang capital; together with Li Qiong, former military training commissioner of Mingzhou, he reached Zhengzhou, and the garrison troops pressed him to patrol within the city against outside bandits, calling him "King of Zheng."

units.zh: 時有嵩山賊帥張遇，領眾萬餘，於僧眾得梁朝故嗣密王朱乙，遂推為天子，取嵩山神冠冕之服以衣之。
units.en: At that time Zhang Yu, a bandit chief on Mount Song, led more than ten thousand men. Among the monks he found Zhu Yi, the former heir of Liang's Secret Prince, proclaimed him emperor, and dressed him in the ceremonial regalia kept for the Mount Song spirit.
units.literal: At that time the bandit chief Zhang Yu of Mount Song led more than ten thousand men; among the monks he obtained Zhu Yi, the former heir of the Secret Prince of Liang, and set him up as Son of Heaven, taking the crown and robes of the Mount Song spirit and clothing him in them.

units.zh: 張遇以其眾攻鄭州，太與李瓊擊之，賊眾敗走，瓊中流矢而死。
units.en: Zhang Yu attacked Zhengzhou with his followers. Tai and Li Qiong met them, routed the bandits, and Qiong was killed by an arrow.
units.literal: Zhang Yu attacked Zhengzhou with his forces; Tai and Li Qiong struck them, the bandits were defeated and fled, and Qiong was struck by a flying arrow and died.

units.zh: 太乃括率郡中財物以賞軍士，因誘之欲同西去，其眾不從，太乃潛奔於洛陽。
units.en: Tai then seized the commandery's wealth to reward the troops and tried to lure them west with him, but they refused. He slipped away to Luoyang in secret.
units.literal: Tai then gathered the wealth of the commandery to reward the soldiers and tried to entice them to go west with him; the troops would not follow, and Tai secretly fled to Luoyang.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：戍兵既失太，反譖太於契丹，雲脅我為亂。
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that after Tai left, the garrison slandered him to the Khitan, claiming he had forced them into rebellion.
units.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror records: Once the garrison troops had lost Tai, they in turn slandered Tai to the Khitan, saying he had forced them into rebellion.

units.zh: 太遣子師朗自訴於契丹，契丹殺之。）〉
units.en: Tai sent his son Shilang to plead his case to the Khitan, and they killed the boy.)
units.literal: Tai sent his son Shilang to plead with the Khitan on his own behalf, and the Khitan killed him.)

units.zh: 及劉晞南走許州，太殺晞牙校李暉，入河南府行留守事。
units.en: When Liu Xi fled south to Xu Prefecture, Tai killed Xi's adjutant Li Hui and entered Henan Prefecture to serve as acting regent.
units.literal: When Liu Xi fled south to Xu Prefecture, Tai killed Xi's adjutant Li Hui and entered Henan Prefecture to act as regent.

units.zh: 既而嵩山賊帥張遇殺嗣密王，傳首於太，懸於洛市。
units.en: Soon the bandit chief Zhang Yu killed the false emperor and sent his head to Tai, who displayed it in the Luoyang market.
units.literal: Before long the bandit chief Zhang Yu of Mount Song killed the heir of the Secret Prince and sent his head to Tai, who hung it in the Luoyang market.

units.zh: 又有伊闕賊帥自稱天子，領眾萬餘，將入洛城，集郊壇之上，太率兵數百人逆擊，破之，賊眾遂潰。
units.en: Another bandit chief at Yique proclaimed himself emperor and gathered more than ten thousand men on the suburban altar, ready to enter Luoyang. Tai led several hundred men against them, routed them, and the bandits fled.
units.literal: There was also a bandit chief of Yique who called himself Son of Heaven, led more than ten thousand men, and was about to enter Luoyang; they gathered on the suburban altar mound. Tai led several hundred troops to meet them head-on, defeated them, and the bandits then scattered.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》引實錄《方太傳》云：劉禧走許田，復有潁陽妖巫，姓朱，號嗣密王，誓眾於洛南天壇，號萬餘人。
units.en: (Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror, citing the Veritable Records biography of Fang Tai, records that Liu Xi fled to Xutian and that a sorcerer of Yingyang surnamed Zhu, calling himself heir of the Secret Prince, mustered followers at Luoyang's southern celestial altar and claimed more than ten thousand men.
units.literal: (Examination of Differences in the Comprehensive Mirror, citing the Veritable Records biography of Fang Tai, records: Liu Xi fled to Xutian; again there was a sorcerer of Yingyang, surname Zhu, who called himself heir of the Secret Prince, mustered followers at the southern celestial altar of Luoyang, and claimed more than ten thousand men.

units.zh: 太帥部曲與朝士輩虛張旗幟，一舉而逐之，洛師遂安。）〉
units.en: Tai led his personal troops and court officials in a show of banners, drove them off in one stroke, and Luoyang was pacified.)〉
units.literal: Tai led his personal troops and court officials in a false display of banners and flags, drove them off in one stroke, and the Luoyang army was then pacified.)〉

units.zh: 河陽武行德遣使召太，詐言欲推之為帥，尋為行德所害。
units.en: Wu Xingde of Heyang sent for Tai, pretending he would make him commander, but soon had him killed.
units.literal: Wu Xingde of Heyang sent a messenger to summon Tai, falsely saying he wished to set him up as commander, but soon Tai was killed by Xingde.

units.zh: 何建，其先回鶻人也，代居雲、朔間。
units.en: He Jian was descended from Uyghurs who had lived for generations between Yun and Shuo.
units.literal: He Jian—his ancestors were Uyghurs who for generations dwelt between Yun and Shuo.

units.zh: 祖慶，父懷福，俱事後唐武皇為小校。
units.en: His grandfather Qing and his father Huaifu had both served Later Tang's Martial Emperor as junior officers.
units.literal: His grandfather Qing and his father Huaifu both served Later Tang's Martial Emperor as junior officers.

units.zh: 建少以謹厚隸於高祖帳下，以掌廄為役，及即位，累典禁軍，
units.en: As a youth Jian, known for prudence and steadiness, served in Gaozu's tent managing the stables. When Gaozu took the throne, he rose through commands of the palace guard,
units.literal: In youth Jian, for his prudence and steadiness, served under Gaozu's tent in charge of the stables; when Gaozu took the throne, he repeatedly commanded the palace guard,

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：重建初事晉祖為奉德馬軍都指揮使。）〉
units.en: (The Annals of the Nine States records that He Jian (written Chong Jian in that source) first served the Jin founder as commander of the Fengde Palace Guard cavalry.)
units.literal: (The Annals of the Nine States records: At first Chong Jian served the Jin founder as commander of the Fengde Palace Guard cavalry.)

units.zh: 遙領歡、睦二郡。
units.en: He held titular command of Huan and Mu prefectures.
units.literal: He held titular command of Huan and Mu prefectures.

units.zh: 天福中，自曹州刺史遷延州兵馬留後，尋正授旄鉞。
units.en: During Tianfu he moved from prefect of Cao to acting regent of Yanzhou and soon received full military commission.
units.literal: During Tianfu he moved from prefect of Caozhou to acting regent of Yanzhou's army and horses, and soon received the full commissioner's baton and axe.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：延州節度使丁審琪殘暴貪冒，蕃部苦之。
units.en: (The Annals of the Nine States records that Yanzhou military commissioner Ding Shenqi was cruel and greedy and that the frontier tribes suffered under him.
units.literal: (The Annals of the Nine States records: Ding Shenqi, military commissioner of Yanzhou, was cruel, violent, and greedy; the frontier tribes suffered under him.

units.zh: 重建以所部兵攻其城，審琪遁去，晉祖即以重建權節度兵馬留後，下車諭以威福，邊民安堵，就加彰武軍節度使。）〉
units.en: He Jian attacked the city with his troops; Shenqi fled; the Jin founder made Jian acting regent of Yanzhou; on taking office he taught them the limits of power, the frontier people were pacified, and he was then made military commissioner of the Zhangwu Army.)〉
units.literal: Chong Jian attacked his city with the troops under his command; Shenqi fled; the Jin founder at once made Chong Jian acting regent of the circuit's army and horses; on taking office he instructed them in authority and favor, the frontier people were settled in peace, and he was then made military commissioner of the Zhangwu Army.)〉

units.zh: 數年之間，歷涇、鄧、貝、澶、孟五鎮節度使，
units.en: Within a few years he served in turn as military commissioner of Jing, Deng, Bei, Chan, and Meng,
units.literal: Within a few years he served in turn as military commissioner of the five circuits Jing, Deng, Bei, Chan, and Meng,

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：皆以廉儉簡易稱。）〉
units.en: (The Annals of the Nine States records that in every post he was praised for frugality and plain dealing.)〉
units.literal: (The Annals of the Nine States records: In all cases he was praised for frugality, simplicity, and plain dealing.)〉

units.zh: 累官至檢校太傅。
units.en: He eventually rose to Acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: He rose through offices to Acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 開運三年，移鎮秦州。
units.en: In the third year of Kaiyun he was transferred to Qinzhou.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaiyun he was transferred to command Qinzhou.

units.zh: 是冬，契丹入汴，其主遣人賫詔以賜建，建憤然謂將吏曰：「吾事石氏二主，累擁戎旃，人臣之榮，亦已極矣。
units.en: That winter the Khitan entered Bian, and their ruler sent an edict to honor Jian. Jian said angrily to his officers, "I have served two lords of the Shi house and held command after command. A subject's glory could go no further.
units.literal: That winter the Khitan entered Bian, and their ruler sent someone bearing an edict to bestow favors on Jian. Jian said angrily to his generals and officials, "I have served the two lords of the Shi clan, repeatedly holding the military banner; the glory of a subject could not go further.

units.zh: 今日不能率兵赴難，豈可受制於契丹乎！」
units.en: If I cannot march to the dynasty's rescue today, how can I submit to the Khitan?"
units.literal: Today, unable to lead troops to the state's rescue, how can I submit to control by the Khitan!"

units.zh: 即遣使賫表與其地送款於蜀，孟昶待之甚厚，偽加同平章事，依前秦州節度使。
units.en: He sent envoys with a memorial and his territory to submit to Shu. Meng Chang received him generously, gave him the false title of Vice Grand Councilor, and left him military commissioner of Qinzhou.
units.literal: He at once sent envoys bearing a memorial and his territory to offer submission to Shu; Meng Chang treated him very generously, falsely made him Vice Grand Councilor of the Tong rank, and left him as before military commissioner of Qinzhou.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：時固鎮與鳳州未平，重建悉經略討平之。）〉
units.en: (The Annals of the Nine States records that Guzhen and Fengzhou were not yet pacified and that He Jian subdued them all.)〉
units.literal: (The Annals of the Nine States records: At that time Guzhen and Fengzhou were not yet pacified; Chong Jian planned and subdued them all.)〉

units.zh: 歲餘，移閬州保寧軍節度使，
units.en: After more than a year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Baoning Army at Langzhou,
units.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to be military commissioner of the Baoning Army at Langzhou,

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：昶大舉兵北伐，遣張虔釗出大散關，以重建為招討使，由隴州路以進師，無功而還。）〉
units.en: (The Annals of the Nine States records that Chang launched a major northern campaign, sent Zhang Qianzhao through Dasanguan, and made He Jian pacification commissioner to advance by the Longzhou route, but achieved nothing and returned.)〉
units.literal: (The Annals of the Nine States records: Chang launched a great northern campaign, sent Zhang Qianzhao out through Dasanguan, and made Chong Jian pacification commissioner to advance by the Longzhou route; he achieved nothing and returned.)〉

units.zh: 加偽官至中書令，後卒於蜀。
units.en: He was given the false rank of Director of the Secretariat and later died in Shu.
units.literal: He was given the false court rank of Director of the Secretariat and later died in Shu.

units.zh: 張廷蘊，字德樞，開封襄邑人也。
units.en: Zhang Tingyun, courtesy name Deshu, was from Xiangyi in Kaifeng.
units.literal: Zhang Tingyun, courtesy name Deshu, was a native of Xiangyi in Kaifeng.

units.zh: 祖立，贈驍衛將軍。
units.en: His grandfather Li was posthumously made general of the Valiant Guard.
units.literal: His grandfather Li was posthumously given the rank of general of the Valiant Guard.

units.zh: 父及，贈光祿大夫。
units.en: His father Ji was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.
units.literal: His father Ji was posthumously given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Brightness.

units.zh: 廷蘊少勇捷，始隸宣武軍為伍長，唐天復中，奔太原，武皇收於帳下為小校。
units.en: As a youth Tingyun was brave and quick. He first served in the Xuanwu Army as a squad leader. In Tang's Tianfu era (901–904) he fled to Taiyuan, and the Martial Emperor took him into his tent as a junior officer.
units.literal: In youth Tingyun was brave and quick; he first served in the Xuanwu Army as a squad leader. In Tang's Tianfu era (901–904) he fled to Taiyuan, and the Martial Emperor took him into his tent as a junior officer.

units.zh: 及莊宗救上黨，戰柏鄉，攻薊門，下邢、魏，皆從之。
units.en: He followed Zhuangzong in the relief of Shangdang, the battle at Baixiang, the assault on Jimen, and the capture of Xing and Wei.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong relieved Shangdang, fought at Baixiang, attacked Jimen, and took Xing and Wei, he followed in all cases.

units.zh: 後戰於莘縣及胡柳陂，繼為流矢所中，金瘡之痕，盈於面首。
units.en: Later, at Shen County and Huliupo, he was hit again and again by arrows until blade scars covered his face and head.
units.literal: Later he fought at Shen County and Huliupo, was repeatedly struck by flying arrows, and scars from blade wounds covered his face and head.

units.zh: 莊宗寵之，統御營黃甲軍，常在左右，累加檢校兵部尚書、帳前步軍都虞候，充諸軍濠寨使。
units.en: Zhuangzong favored him, gave him command of the Imperial Camp Yellow Armor Army, and kept him at his side. He rose to Acting Minister of War and chief adjutant of the infantry before the tent and served as moat-camp commissioner for all armies.
units.literal: Zhuangzong favored him, put him in command of the Imperial Camp Yellow Armor Army, kept him constantly at his side, repeatedly promoted him to Acting Minister of War and chief adjutant of the infantry before the tent, and appointed him moat-camp commissioner for all armies.

units.zh: 同光初，從明宗收汶陽，加檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博三城巡檢使。
units.en: Early in Tongguang he followed Mingzong in recovering Wenyang, was made Acting Vice Minister of State Affairs, and became patrol commissioner of Weibo's three cities.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he followed Mingzong in recovering Wenyang, was made Acting Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and appointed patrol commissioner of the three cities of Weibo.

units.zh: 時皇后劉氏在鄴，每縱其下擾人，廷蘊多斬之，聞者壯焉。
units.en: Empress Liu was then at Ye and often let her followers harass the people. Tingyun executed many of them, to general admiration.
units.literal: At that time Empress Liu was at Ye and often let her followers harass the people; Tingyun frequently executed them, and those who heard of it admired him.

units.zh: 梁平，承詔入覲，改帳前都指揮使兼左右羽林都虞候。
units.en: After Liang fell he was summoned to court and made commander before the tent with concurrent chief adjutant of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.
units.literal: When Liang was pacified he received orders to attend court and was changed to commander before the tent with concurrent chief adjutant of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.

units.zh: 會李繼韜故將楊立叛，詔遣明宗為招討使，元行欽為都部署，廷蘊為前鋒。
units.en: When Yang Li, a former officer of Li Jitao, rebelled, Mingzong was sent as pacification commissioner, Yuan Xingqin as overall deployment commander, and Tingyun as vanguard.
units.literal: When Yang Li, a former officer of Li Jitao, rebelled, an edict sent Mingzong as pacification commissioner, Yuan Xingqin as overall deployment commander, and Tingyun as vanguard.

units.zh: 軍至上黨，日已暝矣，憩軍方定，廷蘊首率勁兵百餘輩，逾洫坎城而上，守陴者不能禦，尋斬關延諸軍入焉。
units.en: The army reached Shangdang at dusk, just as the troops were settling in, when Tingyun led more than a hundred picked men over the moat and up the wall. The defenders could not stop them. He cut through the gate and let the whole army in.
units.literal: The army reached Shangdang; the day was already dark and the resting troops had just settled when Tingyun first led more than a hundred picked soldiers over the moat and up the wall; the defenders on the parapet could not resist, and soon he cut through the gate and drew the whole army in.

units.zh: 明宗、行欽達明而始至，其城已下，明宗甚慊之。
units.en: Mingzong and Xingqin arrived at dawn to find the city already taken. Mingzong was deeply pleased with him.
units.literal: Mingzong and Xingqin arrived at dawn and only then came up; the city was already taken, and Mingzong was very pleased with him.

units.zh: 軍還，改左右羽林都指揮使，加檢校司空，行申州刺史。
units.en: When the army returned he was made commander of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards, Acting Minister of Works, and acting prefect of Shenzhou.
units.literal: When the army returned he was made commander of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards, given the rank of Acting Minister of Works, and acted as prefect of Shenzhou.

units.zh: 同光末，從皇子魏王繼岌伐蜀，授行營中軍都指揮使。
units.en: Late in Tongguang he followed Imperial Prince Wei Wang Jiji against Shu and was made commander of the campaign's center army.
units.literal: At the end of Tongguang he followed Imperial Prince Wei Wang Jiji in the campaign against Shu and was appointed commander of the campaign headquarters center army.

units.zh: 蜀平，明宗嗣位，遷懷州刺史，賜竭忠建策興復功臣，加檢校司徒。
units.en: After Shu fell and Mingzong took the throne, he became prefect of Huai, was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty in Planning Restoration, and was made Acting Minister of Education.
units.literal: When Shu was pacified and Mingzong succeeded to the throne, he was moved to prefect of Huaizhou, granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty in Planning Restoration, and made Acting Minister of Education.

units.zh: 旋移金州防禦使，加檢校太保，繼授潁州團練使、沿淮招安使。
units.en: He was soon made defense commissioner of Jin, Acting Grand Guardian, then military training commissioner of Ying and pacification commissioner along the Huai.
units.literal: Soon he was moved to defense commissioner of Jinzhou, made Acting Grand Guardian, and then appointed military training commissioner of Yingzhou and pacification commissioner along the Huai.

units.zh: 應順中，轉隴州防禦使。
units.en: During Yingshun he became defense commissioner of Longzhou.
units.literal: During Yingshun he was transferred to defense commissioner of Longzhou.

units.zh: 清泰中，進封清河郡公。
units.en: During Qingtai he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.
units.literal: During Qingtai he was advanced to Duke of Qinghe commandery.

units.zh: 高祖即位，入為右龍武統軍，遷絳州防禦使。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he entered court as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army and became defense commissioner of Jiang.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he entered court as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army and was moved to defense commissioner of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，領左軍衛上將軍，加特進。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded he became senior general of the Left Army Guard with the special advance rank.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded he led as senior general of the Left Army Guard and was given the special advance rank.

units.zh: 開運三年冬，以老病求歸於宋城，明年卒於家，時年六十九。
units.en: In the winter of the third year of Kaiyun he asked to retire to Songcheng because of age and illness. The next year he died at home, aged sixty-nine.
units.literal: In the winter of the third year of Kaiyun, citing old age and illness he asked to return to Songcheng; the next year he died at home, aged sixty-nine.

units.zh: 廷蘊所識不過數字，而性重文士。
units.en: Tingyun knew barely a few written characters, yet he greatly valued scholars.
units.literal: Tingyun recognized no more than a few characters, yet by nature he valued literary men.

units.zh: 下汶陽日，首獲鄆帥戴思遠判官趙鳳，訊之曰：「爾狀貌必儒人也，勿隱其情。」
units.en: When Wenyang fell he captured Zhao Feng, judge-advocate to Yan's military commissioner Dai Siyuan, and said, "You look like a scholar. Do not hide the truth."
units.literal: On the day Wenyang fell he first captured Zhao Feng, judge-advocate to Yan military commissioner Dai Siyuan, and questioned him, saying, "Your appearance must be that of a Confucian—do not hide the truth."

units.zh: 鳳具言之，尋引薦於明宗，明宗令送赴行臺，尋除鳳翰林學士。
units.en: Feng told him everything. Tingyun recommended him to Mingzong, who sent him to headquarters and soon made him a Hanlin academician.
units.literal: Feng told him everything, and soon Tingyun recommended him to Mingzong; Mingzong ordered him sent to the field headquarters, and before long Feng was made Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 及鳳入相，頗與廷蘊相洽，數言於近臣安重誨，重誨亦以廷蘊苦戰出於諸將之右，力保薦之。
units.en: When Feng became chief minister he remained close to Tingyun and repeatedly spoke for him to An Chonghui, who also strongly recommended him because his fighting record surpassed the other generals.
units.literal: When Feng entered the chancellery he was quite close to Tingyun and repeatedly spoke of him to the intimate minister An Chonghui; Chonghui also, because Tingyun's hard fighting stood above the other generals, strongly recommended him.

units.zh: 明宗以廷蘊取潞之日，不能讓功於己，故恒蓄宿忿，至使廷蘊位竟不至方鎮，亦命矣夫！
units.en: Mingzong, because Tingyun would not share credit for taking Lu, always harbored a grudge, so Tingyun never reached a circuit command. Such was fate.
units.literal: Mingzong, because on the day Tingyun took Lu he would not yield the credit to him, always harbored an old resentment, so that Tingyun in the end never reached a circuit command—fate indeed!

units.zh: 廷蘊歷七郡，家無餘積，年老耋期，終於牖下，良可嘉也。
units.en: Tingyun served in seven commanderies yet left no surplus wealth. He lived to great age and died at home—truly admirable.
units.literal: Tingyun served in seven commanderies yet his household had no surplus accumulation; in old age he reached extreme longevity and died beneath his own window—truly admirable.

units.zh: 長子光被，歷通事舍人。
units.en: His eldest son Guangbei served as courier-attendant.
units.literal: His eldest son Guangbei served in turn as courier-attendant.

units.zh: 郭延魯，字德興，沁州綿上人也。
units.en: Guo Yanlu, courtesy name Dexing, was from Mianshang in Qin.
units.literal: Guo Yanlu, courtesy name Dexing, was a native of Mianshang in Qinzhou.

units.zh: 父饒，後唐武皇時，以軍功嘗為本郡守，凡九年，有遺愛焉。
units.en: His father Rao had served as prefect of their home commandery for nine years under Later Tang's Martial Emperor and left a legacy of affection.
units.literal: His father Rao, during Later Tang's Martial Emperor, once served as prefect of his home commandery for military merit, for nine years in all, and left a legacy of affection.

units.zh: 延魯少有勇，善用槊，莊宗以舊將之子，擢為保衛軍使，頻戍塞下，捍契丹有功。
units.en: Yanlu was brave from youth and a skilled spearman. Zhuangzong, because he was the son of an old general, made him commissioner of the Baowei army. He often garrisoned the frontier and won merit repelling the Khitan.
units.literal: Yanlu was brave from youth and skilled with the spear. Zhuangzong, because he was the son of an old general, promoted him to commissioner of the Baowei army. He often garrisoned the frontier and had merit in repelling the Khitan.

units.zh: 及即位，賜協謀定亂功臣，加檢校兵部尚書、右神武都指揮都知兵馬使。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne he received the title Meritorious Minister of Cooperative Counsel and Pacifying Rebellion and was made Acting Minister of War and overall commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard with charge of troops and horses.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was granted the title Meritorious Minister of Cooperative Counsel and Pacifying Rebellion and made Acting Minister of War and overall commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard with charge of troops and horses.

units.zh: 天成中，汴州朱守殷叛，延魯從車駕東幸，至其地，坎壘先登。
units.en: During Tiancheng, when Zhu Shouyin of Bian rebelled, Yanlu followed the emperor east and was first to scale the ramparts on arrival.
units.literal: During Tiancheng, when Zhu Shouyin of Bianzhou rebelled, Yanlu followed the imperial carriage east and, on reaching the place, was first to scale the ramparts.

units.zh: 守殷平，以功授汴州步軍都指揮使，加檢校尚書左僕射。
units.en: After Shouyin was suppressed, Yanlu was made commander of the Bian infantry for his service and promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: When Shouyin was pacified, Yanlu was made commander of the Bianzhou infantry for his merit and promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 長興中，累加檢校司徒，歷天雄軍北京馬步軍都校，遙領梧州刺史。
units.en: During Changxing he rose to Acting Minister of Education, served as overall commander of the Tianxiong Army northern capital horse-and-foot forces, and held titular command of Wu.
units.literal: During Changxing he was further promoted to Acting Minister of Education, served as overall commander of the Tianxiong Army northern capital horse-and-foot forces, and held titular command of Wuzhou.

units.zh: 清泰中，遷復州刺史，正俸之外，未嘗斂貸，庶事就理，一郡賴焉。
units.en: During Qingtai he became prefect of Fu. Beyond his regular salary he never collected loans, put affairs in order, and the whole commandery relied on him.
units.literal: During Qingtai he was transferred to prefect of Fu. Beyond his regular salary he never collected loans; all affairs were put in order, and the whole commandery relied on him.

units.zh: 秩滿，百姓上章舉留，朝廷嘉之。
units.en: When his term ended the people petitioned to keep him, and the court praised him.
units.literal: When his term ended the people submitted a memorial asking that he remain, and the court praised him.

units.zh: 高祖即位，遷單州刺史，加檢校太保，賜輸誠奉義忠烈功臣。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he became prefect of Shan, Acting Grand Guardian, and received the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Submission, Righteous Service, and Fierce Loyalty.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne Yanlu was transferred to prefect of Shan, promoted to Acting Grand Guardian, and granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Submission, Righteous Service, and Fierce Loyalty.

units.zh: 到任逾月，以疾卒於理所，時年四十七。
units.en: Little more than a month after taking office he died of illness at his post, aged forty-seven.
units.literal: A little more than a month after reaching his post he died of illness in the government offices, aged forty-seven.

units.zh: 詔贈太傅。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the title grand tutor.
units.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 郭金海，本突厥之族。
units.en: Guo Jinhai was of Turkic descent.
units.literal: Guo Jinhai was originally of Turkic stock.

units.zh: 少侍昭義節度使李嗣昭，常從征伐。
units.en: As a youth he served Li Sizhao, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, and often followed him on campaign.
units.literal: In youth he attended Li Sizhao, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, and often followed him on campaigns.

units.zh: 金海好酒，所為不法，自潞州過山東，入邢洺界為劫盜，嗣昭雖知之，然惜其拳勇，每優容之。
units.en: Jinhai loved wine and often acted outside the law. Leaving Luzhou for Shandong he robbed in Xing and Ming. Sizhao knew it but valued his fighting skill and indulged him.
units.literal: Jinhai loved wine and his conduct was unlawful; passing from Luzhou through Shandong he entered the territory of Xing and Ming as a robber. Sizhao knew it, yet valued his fist-fighting courage and always indulged him.

units.zh: 天祐中，累職至昭義親騎指揮使。
units.en: During Tianyou he rose to commander of Zhaoyi's personal cavalry.
units.literal: During Tianyou he rose through offices to commander of the Zhaoyi personal cavalry.

units.zh: 同光二年，遷本道馬軍都指揮使。
units.en: In the second year of Tongguang he became commander of the circuit cavalry.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he was moved to commander of the circuit's cavalry.

units.zh: 天成初，入為捧聖指揮使。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he entered court as commander of the Upholding Sagely Corps.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he entered court as commander of the Upholding Sagely Corps.

units.zh: 長興三年，改護聖都虞候。
units.en: In the third year of Changxing he became chief adjutant of the Guarding Sagely Corps.
units.literal: In the third year of Changxing he was changed to chief adjutant of the Guarding Sagely Corps.

units.zh: 天福二年，從王師討範延光於魏州，以功轉本軍都指揮使，領黃州刺史。
units.en: In the second year of Tianfu he marched against Fan Yanguang at Weizhou and, for his service, became commander of his corps with titular command of Huangzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he followed the imperial army in attacking Fan Yanguang at Weizhou and, for merit, was transferred to commander of his corps with titular command of Huangzhou.

units.zh: 高祖幸鄴，宣金海領部兵巡檢東京。
units.en: When Gaozu visited Ye he ordered Jinhai to patrol the Eastern Capital with his troops.
units.literal: When Gaozu visited Ye he ordered Jinhai to lead his unit in patrolling the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 其年十一月，安從進謀犯闕，金海為襄州道行營先鋒都指揮使，與李建崇等同於唐州湖陽遇從進軍萬餘人，金海以一旅之眾突擊，大敗之，策勛授檢校太保、商州刺史，俄移慶州。
units.en: That November, when An Congjin rebelled, Jinhai was vanguard commander on the Xiangzhou route. With Li Jianchong and others he met Congjin's army of more than ten thousand at Huyang in Tangzhou and routed them with a single brigade. He was made Acting Grand Guardian and prefect of Shang, then soon transferred to Qing.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of that year An Congjin plotted to violate the capital; Jinhai was vanguard commander of the Xiangzhou route campaign headquarters. Together with Li Jianchong and others he met Congjin's army of more than ten thousand at Huyang in Tangzhou; Jinhai with a single brigade charged and routed them. For recorded merit he was made Acting Grand Guardian and prefect of Shangzhou, and soon moved to Qingzhou.

units.zh: 秩滿歸闕，途中遇疾而卒，年六十一。
units.en: When his term ended he returned to court, fell ill on the road, and died at sixty-one.
units.literal: When his term ended he returned to court, fell ill on the road, and died, aged sixty-one.

units.zh: 〈（《洛陽縉紳舊聞記》：從進與金海相遇於花山。
units.en: (Old Reports Heard among the Gentry of Luoyang records that Congjin and Jinhai met at Huashan.
units.literal: (Old Reports Heard among the Gentry of Luoyang records: Congjin and Jinhai met at Huashan.

units.zh: 金海蕃將，善用槍，時罕與敵，拳勇過人，喜戰鬥，欲立奇功。
units.en: Jinhai was a frontier general, a master of the spear, rarely matched in his day, surpassingly brave, eager for battle, and hungry for glory.
units.literal: Jinhai was a barbarian general, skilled with the spear, rarely matched in his time, surpassing others in fist-fighting courage, fond of battle, and eager to win extraordinary merit.

units.zh: 兩陣相去數里。
units.en: The two armies stood several li apart.
units.literal: The two battle lines were several li apart.

units.zh: 從進素管騎兵，金海久在麾下，從進亦待之素厚。
units.en: Congjin had long commanded cavalry, and Jinhai had served under him for years. Congjin had always treated him well.
units.literal: Congjin had long commanded cavalry; Jinhai had been under him for a long time, and Congjin had always treated him generously.

units.zh: 乃躍馬引數百騎乘高，去金海陣數百步，厲聲呼「郭金海」。
units.en: He spurred his horse, led several hundred horsemen to high ground a few hundred paces from Jinhai's line, and shouted, "Guo Jinhai!"
units.literal: He then spurred his horse, led several hundred horsemen to high ground several hundred paces from Jinhai's line, and shouted loudly, "Guo Jinhai!"

units.zh: 金海獨鞭馬出於陣數十步，免胄側身，高聲自稱曰「金海」。
units.en: Jinhai rode out alone several dozen paces from his line, removed his helmet, turned sideways, and shouted back, "Jinhai!"
units.literal: Jinhai alone whipped his horse out from the line several dozen paces, removed his helmet and turned sideways, and loudly called his own name, "Jinhai."

units.zh: 從進又前行數十步，勞之曰：「金海安否？
units.en: Congjin rode forward another few dozen paces and called, "Jinhai, are you well?
units.literal: Congjin advanced another several dozen paces and greeted him, saying, "Jinhai, are you well?

units.zh: 我素待爾厚，略不知恩，今日敢來共我相殺？」
units.en: I have always treated you well, yet you show no gratitude. Today you dare come and fight me?"
units.literal: I have always treated you generously, yet you scarcely know gratitude—today you dare come and fight me to the death?"

units.zh: 金海應聲答曰：「官家好看大王，負大王甚事，大王今日反？
units.en: Jinhai answered at once, "The Son of Heaven treats you well. What wrong did you suffer that you rebel today?
units.literal: Jinhai answered at once, "The Son of Heaven treats the Great King well—what wrong did the Great King suffer that he rebels today?

units.zh: 金海舊事大王，乞與大王一箭地，大王回去，若不去，吃取金海槍。」
units.en: I once served you. Give me an arrow-shot of ground and go back. If you do not, taste my spear."
units.literal: Jinhai once served the Great King—beg leave for an arrow-shot of ground; Great King, go back. If you do not go, taste Jinhai's spear."

units.zh: 言訖，援槍鞭馬，疾趨其陣。
units.en: With that he seized his spear, whipped his horse, and galloped back to his line.
units.literal: When he had spoken he seized his spear, whipped his horse, and galloped back to his line.

units.zh: 從進懼，躍馬而進，師遂相接，大為金海、焦繼勛摧敗。
units.en: Congjin, alarmed, charged forward, the armies clashed, and Jinhai and Jiao Jixun routed him completely.
units.literal: Congjin was afraid, spurred his horse forward, and the armies then clashed; Congjin's force was greatly crushed by Jinhai and Jiao Jixun.

units.zh: 奏到，晉祖大喜，賞賜有差。
units.en: When the report reached court, Jin Zu was delighted and rewarded them generously.
units.literal: When the report arrived Jin Zu was greatly pleased and bestowed rewards in varying measure.

units.zh: 從進自此喪氣，嬰城自固，王師為連城重塹以守之。
units.en: From then on Congjin lost heart, shut himself in the city, and the imperial army built linked walls and deep trenches to hold him there.
units.literal: From this Congjin lost heart, shut himself in the city and held firm, and the imperial army built linked walls and deep moats to besiege him.

units.zh: 月餘，王師攻城，城上矢下如雨，王師被傷者眾。
units.en: After more than a month the imperial army assaulted the city. Arrows fell like rain from the walls and many soldiers were wounded.
units.literal: After more than a month the imperial army assaulted the city; arrows fell like rain from the walls, and many of the imperial troops were wounded.

units.zh: 是日，金海為飛矢集身，扶傷歸營。
units.en: That day Jinhai was struck by arrows all over his body and was carried back to camp wounded.
units.literal: That day Jinhai was struck all over by flying arrows and was helped back to camp wounded.

units.zh: 明日，從進用計汙金海，欲使朝廷疑之。
units.en: The next day Congjin tried to smear Jinhai and make the court suspect him.
units.literal: The next day Congjin used a stratagem to sully Jinhai, wishing to make the court suspect him.

units.zh: 以金瓶貯酒，金合盛藥，以索懸之，城上呼「郭金海」。
units.en: He hung a golden bottle of wine and a golden box of medicine from ropes and called down from the wall, "Guo Jinhai!"
units.literal: He put wine in a golden bottle and medicine in a golden box, hung them by a rope, and from atop the wall called "Guo Jinhai."

units.zh: 金海知之，力疾扶創而往。
units.en: Jinhai heard the call, forced himself up despite his wounds, and went.
units.literal: Jinhai knew of it, forced himself despite illness and wounds, and went.

units.zh: 城上勞金海曰：「大王知爾中箭創甚，賜爾金瓶金合酒與風藥。」
units.en: From the wall they called down, "The Great King knows you were badly wounded and sends you this golden bottle and box of wine and medicine."
units.literal: From atop the wall they greeted Jinhai, saying, "The Great King knows you were badly wounded by arrows and bestows on you this golden bottle and golden box of wine and cooling medicine."

units.zh: 金海目不知書，惟利是貪，取瓶與合歸營，且不聞於元戎。
units.en: Jinhai could not read and cared only for gain. He took the bottle and box back to camp without telling the commander.
units.literal: Jinhai could not read and cared only for profit; he took the bottle and box back to camp and did not report it to the commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 元戎等疑之，乃馳驛奏。
units.en: The commanders grew suspicious and sent an urgent report to court.
units.literal: The commander-in-chief and others suspected him and sent a fast dispatch to report it.

units.zh: 晉祖以花山之功，不加罪。
units.en: Because of his victory at Huashan, Jin Zu did not punish him.
units.literal: Jin Zu, because of the merit at Huashan, did not punish him.

units.zh: 城下，就除金州團練，並其兵於他部。
units.en: When the city fell he was made military training commissioner of Jin on the spot, and his troops were transferred to another command.
units.literal: When the city fell he was made on the spot military training commissioner of Jinzhou, and his troops were merged into another unit.

units.zh: 金海之任，居常悒悒不樂，至於捐館。）〉
units.en: In his new post he was constantly depressed until he died.)
units.literal: In Jinhai's post he was constantly depressed and unhappy, until he gave up the lodge.)

units.zh: 劉處讓，字德謙，滄州人也。
units.en: Liu Churang, courtesy name Deqian, was from Cangzhou.
units.literal: Liu Churang, courtesy name Deqian, was a native of Cangzhou.

units.zh: 祖信，累贈太子少保。
units.en: His grandfather Xin was repeatedly posthumously made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: His grandfather Xin was repeatedly posthumously given the rank of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 父喻，累贈太子少師。
units.en: His father Yu was repeatedly posthumously made Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: His father Yu was repeatedly posthumously given the rank of Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 梁貞明初，張萬進帥兗州，處讓事之，為親校。
units.en: Early in Liang's Zhenming era, when Zhang Wanjin commanded Yanzhou, Churang served him as a personal attendant.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming under Liang, Zhang Wanjin commanded Yanzhou; Churang served him as a personal attendant.

units.zh: 萬進據城叛，梁遣大將劉鄩討之。
units.en: Wanjin rebelled and held the city. Liang sent the great general Liu Yan against him.
units.literal: Wanjin held the city in rebellion, and Liang sent the great general Liu Yan to attack him.

units.zh: 時唐莊宗屯軍於麻口渡，萬進密遣處讓乞師於莊宗，莊宗未即應之，乃於軍門截耳曰：「主帥急難，使我告援，茍不得請，死亦何避。」
units.en: Zhuangzong of Tang was then encamped at Makou Ford. Wanjin secretly sent Churang to beg for troops. Zhuangzong hesitated, so Churang cut off his ear at the army gate and said, "My commander is in peril and sent me to beg aid. If you refuse, I do not fear death."
units.literal: At that time Tang's Zhuangzong had his army encamped at Makou Ford; Wanjin secretly sent Churang to beg troops from Zhuangzong. Zhuangzong did not immediately agree, so at the army gate he cut off his ear and said, "Our commander is in urgent peril and sent me to beg aid; if the request is not granted, what is there to fear in death?"

units.zh: 莊宗義之，將舉兵渡河，俄聞城陷乃止。
units.en: Zhuangzong admired his loyalty and was about to cross the river, but heard the city had already fallen and stopped.
units.literal: Zhuangzong admired his righteousness and was about to lead troops across the river, but soon heard the city had fallen and stopped.

units.zh: 因以墨制授處讓行臺左驍衛將軍，俄改客省副使。
units.en: He then appointed Churang general of the Left Valiant Guard of the field headquarters by informal edict and soon made him deputy commissioner of the Reception Bureau.
units.literal: He therefore granted Churang by informal edict the post of general of the Left Valiant Guard of the field headquarters, and soon changed him to deputy commissioner of the Reception Bureau.

units.zh: 梁平，加檢校兵部尚書，累將命稱旨。
units.en: After Liang fell he was made Acting Minister of War and repeatedly carried out missions to the emperor's satisfaction.
units.literal: When Liang was pacified he was made Acting Minister of War and repeatedly carried out missions to the emperor's satisfaction.

units.zh: 天成初，轉檢校尚書右僕射，依前充職。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he became Acting Vice Minister of State Affairs while keeping his former duties.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was transferred to Acting Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs while continuing his former duties.

units.zh: 歲餘遷引進使。
units.en: After more than a year he became commissioner of introductions.
units.literal: After more than a year he was moved to commissioner of introductions.

units.zh: 長興三年，轉檢校司空、左威衛大將軍，其職如故。
units.en: In the third year of Changxing he became Acting Minister of Works and great general of the Left Awesome Guard while keeping his former duties.
units.literal: In the third year of Changxing he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works and great general of the Left Awesome Guard, his duties remaining as before.

units.zh: 四年，西川孟知祥跋扈，不通朝貢，朝廷方議懷柔，乃遣處讓為官告國信使，復命，轉檢校司徒。
units.en: In the fourth year Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan was defiant and sent no tribute. The court chose conciliation and sent Churang as credentialed envoy with the imperial patent. On his return he was made Acting Minister of Education.
units.literal: In the fourth year Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan was overbearing and did not send court tribute; the court was discussing conciliation and sent Churang as credentialed envoy bearing the imperial patent; on his return he was made Acting Minister of Education.

units.zh: 應順初，授忻州刺史、檢校太保，充西北面都計度使，備北寇也。
units.en: Early in Yingshun he became prefect of Xin, Acting Grand Guardian, and overall planning commissioner on the northwest frontier against northern invaders.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was appointed prefect of Xinzhou and Acting Grand Guardian and served as overall planning commissioner for the northwest frontier to guard against northern invaders.

units.zh: 清泰二年，入為左驍衛大將軍。
units.en: In the second year of Qingtai he entered court as great general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he entered court as great general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

units.zh: 三年夏，魏博屯將張令昭逐其帥以城叛，朝廷命範延光領兵討之，以處讓為河北都轉運使。
units.en: In the summer of the third year Zhang Lingzhao, a Weibo garrison officer, drove out his commander and rebelled. The court sent Fan Yanguang against him and made Churang overall transport commissioner for Hebei.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year the Weibo garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao drove out his commander and rebelled with the city; the court ordered Fan Yanguang to lead troops against him and made Churang overall transport commissioner for Hebei.

units.zh: 及高祖舉義於太原，處讓從至洛陽，乃授宣徽北院使。
units.en: When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Churang followed him to Luoyang and was appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: When Gaozu raised the banner of revolt at Taiyuan, Churang followed him to Luoyang and was then appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 天福二年，轉左監門衛上將軍，充宣徽南院使。
units.en: In the second year of Tianfu he became senior general of the Left Gate Guard and commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was transferred to senior general of the Left Gate Guard and served as commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 範延光之據鄴也，高祖命宣武軍節度使楊光遠領兵討之。
units.en: When Fan Yanguang held Ye, Gaozu ordered Yang Guangyuan, military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, to march against him.
units.literal: When Fan Yanguang held Ye, Gaozu ordered Yang Guangyuan, military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, to lead troops against him.

units.zh: 時處讓奉詔與光遠同參議軍政，會張從賓作亂於河陽，處讓自黎陽分兵討襲，從賓平，復與楊光遠同攻鄴城。
units.en: Churang was ordered to advise Guangyuan on military affairs. When Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang, Churang detached troops from Liyang to suppress him. After Congbin fell he rejoined Yang Guangyuan in the assault on Ye.
units.literal: At that time Churang received orders to deliberate on military affairs together with Guangyuan; when Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang, Churang divided troops from Liyang to strike and suppress him; after Congbin was pacified he again joined Yang Guangyuan in attacking the city of Ye.

units.zh: 四年冬，範延光將謀納款，尚或遲留，處讓首入其城，以禍福諭之，延光乃降，以功加檢校太傅。
units.en: In the winter of the fourth year Fan Yanguang was ready to surrender but still hesitated. Churang was first into the city and persuaded him with talk of fortune and ruin. Yanguang surrendered, and Churang was made Acting Grand Tutor for his service.
units.literal: In the winter of the fourth year Fan Yanguang was about to offer submission but still hesitated; Churang was first to enter his city, instructed him in fortune and disaster, and Yanguang then surrendered; for merit he was made Acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 先是，桑維翰、李崧兼充樞密使，處讓以莊宗已來，樞密使罕有宰臣兼者，因萌心以覬其位。
units.en: Sang Weihan and Li Song had been serving concurrently as commissioners of military affairs. Churang reflected that since Zhuangzong's time few chief ministers had held that post and began to covet it.
units.literal: Earlier Sang Weihan and Li Song had concurrently served as commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Churang, reflecting that since Zhuangzong's time commissioners of military affairs had rarely been chief ministers concurrently, conceived the ambition to covet that post.

units.zh: 及楊光遠討伐鄴城，軍機大事，高祖每命處讓宣達。
units.en: During Yang Guangyuan's campaign against Ye, Gaozu always had Churang convey his orders on major military affairs.
units.literal: When Yang Guangyuan attacked the city of Ye, on great matters of military planning Gaozu always ordered Churang to announce and convey his will.

units.zh: 時光遠恃軍權，多有越體論奏，高祖依違而已，光遠慊之，頻與處讓宴語及之，處讓訴曰：「非聖旨也，皆出維翰等意。」
units.en: Guangyuan then relied on his military power and often sent memorials that overstepped protocol. Gaozu only wavered. Guangyuan resented this and often discussed it with Churang over wine. Churang said, "Those were not the emperor's orders. They came from Weihan and the others."
units.literal: At that time Guangyuan relied on military authority and often submitted memorials overstepping his station; Gaozu only wavered in response. Guangyuan resented this and repeatedly spoke of it with Churang at banquets. Churang complained, "It is not the holy command—it all comes from Weihan and the others."

units.zh: 及楊光遠入朝，遂於高祖前面言執政之失，高祖知其故，不得已乃罷維翰等，以處讓為樞密使。
units.en: When Yang Guangyuan came to court he denounced the chief ministers before Gaozu. Gaozu understood why and had no choice but to dismiss Weihan and the others and make Churang commissioner of military affairs.
units.literal: When Yang Guangyuan entered court he then spoke before Gaozu of the failures of those in power. Gaozu knew the reason and had no choice but to dismiss Weihan and the others and make Churang commissioner of military affairs.

units.zh: 時處讓每有敷奏，高祖多不稱旨，會處讓丁繼母憂，高祖因議罷樞密使，其本院庶事並委宰臣分判。
units.en: Churang's memorials often failed to please Gaozu. When Churang entered mourning for his stepmother, Gaozu used the occasion to abolish the post of military affairs commissioner and divided the bureau's duties among the chief ministers.
units.literal: At that time whenever Churang presented memorials Gaozu often found them not to his liking. When Churang entered mourning for his stepmother, Gaozu took the occasion to discuss abolishing the commissioner of military affairs and entrusted the bureau's routine affairs to the chief ministers for divided judgment.

units.zh: 處讓居喪期年，起復，授彰德軍節度使、澶衛等州觀察處置等使。
units.en: After a year of mourning Churang was recalled and appointed military commissioner of the Zhangde Army and observation and disposition commissioner for Chan, Wei, and related prefectures.
units.literal: Churang remained in mourning for a year, then was recalled to service and appointed military commissioner of the Zhangde Army and observation and disposition commissioner for Chan, Wei, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 處讓勤於公務，孜孜求理，馭吏民不至苛察，人甚便之。
units.en: Churang was diligent in public affairs and tirelessly sought good governance. He governed officials and people without harsh scrutiny, and the people found him very helpful.
units.literal: Churang was diligent in public affairs and tirelessly sought good governance. In governing officials and people he was not harshly scrutinizing, and the people found him very convenient.

units.zh: 高祖幸鄴都，處讓竭家財貢奉，至於薪炭膏沐之細，悉供億焉。
units.en: When Gaozu visited Yedu, Churang spent his household wealth on tribute, even supplying firewood, charcoal, and toiletries.
units.literal: When Gaozu visited Yedu, Churang exhausted his household wealth in tribute, even to the smallest items such as firewood, charcoal, and toiletries, supplying them all.

units.zh: 六年，除右金吾衛上將軍，處讓自以嘗經重任，又歷方鎮，謂其入朝必重要職，一旦除授金吾，有所不足。
units.en: In the sixth year he was made senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard. Churang, having once held weighty office and served in regional commands, expected an important post on entering court and felt the Golden Crow appointment fell short.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was made senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard. Churang felt that, having once held weighty office and also served in regional commands, on entering court he would surely receive an important post; to be appointed to the Golden Crow guard all at once fell short of his expectations.

units.zh: 少帝即位之初，處讓與宰臣言，有協翼之論，覃恩之際，又未擢用。
units.en: Early in the Young Emperor's reign Churang spoke with the chief ministers about assisting the throne, but when broad favors were granted he was passed over again.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Young Emperor's succession Churang spoke with the chief ministers about assisting the throne, but when favors were broadly granted he was again not promoted.

units.zh: 一日至中書，宰臣馮道、趙瑩、李崧、和凝在列，處讓因酒酣，歷詆諸相，道笑而不答。
units.en: One day he came to the Secretariat, where Feng Dao, Zhao Ying, Li Song, and He Ning were in attendance. Drunk, Churang reviled the ministers one by one; Dao only smiled and said nothing.
units.literal: One day he came to the Secretariat, where the chief ministers Feng Dao, Zhao Ying, Li Song, and He Ning were in attendance. Churang, flushed with wine, reviled the ministers one by one; Dao only smiled and did not answer.

units.zh: 月餘稱病。
units.en: After more than a month he pleaded illness.
units.literal: After more than a month he pleaded illness.

units.zh: 八年，從駕歸汴，寄居於封禪寺，遇疾而卒，年六十三。
units.en: In the eighth year he followed the emperor back to Bian and lodged at Fengchan Temple, where he fell ill and died at the age of sixty-three.
units.literal: In the eighth year he followed the imperial carriage back to Bian and lodged at Fengchan Temple, where he fell ill and died, aged sixty-three.

units.zh: 贈太尉，再贈太師。
units.en: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and later Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant and then again Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 子保勛，仕皇朝，位至省郎。
units.en: His son Baoqin served the dynasty and rose to department secretary.
units.literal: His son Baoqin served the imperial dynasty and reached the rank of a department secretary.

units.zh: 李瓊，字隱光，滄州饒安人也。
units.en: Li Qiong, courtesy name Yinguang, was from Rao'an in Cangzhou.
units.literal: Li Qiong, courtesy name Yinguang, was a native of Rao'an in Cangzhou.

units.zh: 少籍本軍為騎士，莊宗平河朔，隸明宗麾下，漸升為小校。
units.en: As a youth he served in the local army as a cavalryman. When Zhuangzong pacified Hebei he entered Mingzong's service and gradually rose to junior officer.
units.literal: In youth he was registered in the local army as a cavalryman; when Zhuangzong pacified Hebei he came under Mingzong's command and gradually rose to junior officer.

units.zh: 同光二年，明宗受詔，以本部兵送糧入薊門，時高祖從行，至涿州與敵相遇，高祖陷於圍中。
units.en: In the second year of Tongguang, Mingzong was ordered to escort grain to Jimen with his troops. Gaozu went with him. At Zhuozhou they met the enemy and Gaozu was surrounded.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongguang Mingzong received orders to escort grain into Jimen with his unit's troops; Gaozu accompanied the march, and at Zhuozhou they met the enemy; Gaozu was trapped in the encirclement.

units.zh: 瓊顧諸軍已退，密牽高祖鐵衣，指東而遁。
units.en: Qiong saw the army had already withdrawn, quietly pulled Gaozu by his armor, pointed east, and fled.
units.literal: Qiong saw that the armies had already withdrawn, secretly pulled Gaozu's iron armor, pointed east, and fled.

units.zh: 至劉李河，為敵所襲，瓊浮水先至南岸，高祖至河中，馬倒，順流而下，瓊以所執長矛援高祖出之，又以所跨馬奉高祖，瓊徒步護之，奔十餘里，乃入涿州。
units.en: At the Liu-Li River they were attacked. Qiong swam across first. Gaozu's horse fell in midstream and he was swept downstream. Qiong pulled him out with his spear, gave him his own horse, and escorted him on foot for more than ten li until they reached Zhuozhou.
units.literal: At the Liu-Li River they were attacked by the enemy; Qiong swam across and reached the south bank first. Gaozu reached mid-river, his horse fell, and he was carried downstream. Qiong used the long spear in his hand to pull Gaozu out, then gave Gaozu the horse he himself had been riding. Qiong protected him on foot, ran more than ten li, and then entered Zhuozhou.

units.zh: 高祖薦於明宗，明宗賞之，尋超授軍職。
units.en: Gaozu recommended him to Mingzong, who rewarded him and soon gave him an exceptional military promotion.
units.literal: Gaozu recommended him to Mingzong; Mingzong rewarded him and soon gave him extraordinary promotion in military office.

units.zh: 同光末，明宗討趙在禮於鄴。
units.en: Late in Tongguang, Mingzong attacked Zhao Zaili at Ye.
units.literal: At the end of Tongguang Mingzong attacked Zhao Zaili at Ye.

units.zh: 鄴軍既變，明宗退至魏縣，遣高祖以騎士三百疾趨汴州。
units.en: When the Ye army mutinied, Mingzong withdrew to Wei County and sent Gaozu with three hundred horsemen to race for Bianzhou.
units.literal: When the Ye army mutinied, Mingzong withdrew to Wei County and sent Gaozu with three hundred horsemen to hurry to Bianzhou.

units.zh: 時莊宗遣騎將西方鄴守其城，高祖憂之，使瓊以勁兵突封丘門而入，高祖踵之，鄴尋歸命，浚郊遂定。
units.en: Zhuangzong had sent the cavalry general Xifang Ye to hold the city. Gaozu sent Qiong with picked troops through Fengqiu Gate; Gaozu followed close behind. Ye soon submitted and the capital suburbs were secured.
units.literal: At that time Zhuangzong sent the cavalry general Xifang Ye to hold the city; Gaozu was worried and had Qiong break in through Fengqiu Gate with picked troops; Gaozu followed close behind; Ye soon submitted, and the suburbs were secured.

units.zh: 及高祖領陜州，奏補雲騎指揮使，俄改侍衛牙隊指揮使。
units.en: When Gaozu took Shanzhou he had Qiong appointed commander of the Cloud Cavalry, and soon made him commander of the palace guard tooth corps.
units.literal: When Gaozu took command of Shanzhou he memorialized to appoint Qiong commander of the Cloud Cavalry, and soon changed him to commander of the palace guard tooth corps.

units.zh: 長興中，從高祖討東川，至劍州，使瓊以部下兵破賊軍數千，身中重創，軍還，改龍武指揮使。
units.en: During Changxing he followed Gaozu against Dongchuan. At Jianzhou Qiong routed several thousand enemy troops with his own men but was gravely wounded. When the army returned he was made commander of the Dragon Martial Corps.
units.literal: During Changxing he followed Gaozu in attacking Dongchuan; at Jianzhou he had Qiong break several thousand bandit troops with the men under his command; Qiong received grave wounds; when the army returned he was made commander of the Dragon Martial Corps.

units.zh: 清泰中，屯雲州，累擒獲契丹人馬，以功改右捧聖軍指揮使。
units.en: During Qingtai he was garrisoned at Yunzhou, repeatedly captured Khitan men and horses, and was made commander of the Right Upholding Sagely Corps for his service.
units.literal: During Qingtai he was garrisoned at Yunzhou, repeatedly captured Khitan men and horses, and for merit was made commander of the Right Upholding Sagely Corps.

units.zh: 唐末帝以瓊元事高祖，乃自塞下移授單州馬步軍副指揮使。
units.en: The Last Emperor of Tang, because Qiong had long served Gaozu, transferred him from the frontier and made him deputy commander of the Shanzhou horse and foot army.
units.literal: The Last Emperor of Tang, because Qiong had long served Gaozu, moved him down from the frontier pass region and appointed him deputy commander of the Shanzhou horse and foot army.

units.zh: 高祖即位，補護聖都指揮使，又念疇昔輟馬導護之力，前後所賜金帛甚厚，但未升爵位，瓊亦郁郁然。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he made Qiong overall commander of the Guarding Sagely Corps. Gaozu remembered how Qiong had given up his horse and escorted him to safety and rewarded him generously with gold and silk, but never raised his noble rank. Qiong grew resentful.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed overall commander of the Guarding Sagely Corps.
